newsitem.title: RUSSIA: DeBakey says Yeltsin had flu but heart normal.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey says Yeltsin had flu but heart normal.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has suffered a bout of flu but his heart is "perfectly normal", Michael DeBakey, the U.S. cardiologist who consulted on Yeltsin's heart surgery, said on Wednesday.

Asked about Yeltsin's shaky physical performance during a visit to Germany last week, DeBakey answered: "No, no. He is doing very well. He developed flu and of course he had to recover from it. His heart is perfectly normal. He is leading a normal life."
Debakey did not say when Yeltsin had suffered from flu and it was the first time the illness had been mentioned. A Kremlin spokesman could offer no immediate comment.
The U.S. surgeon made his brief remarks to reporters during a visit to Russia's second city to accept an award.
Yeltsin, who had quintuple bypass surgery last November and suffered from double pneumonia in January, looked pale and tired last week during talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
He spoke clearly but showed more signs of fatigue than in other recent appearances since he returned to work after his illness two months ago.

Yeltsin flew straight from Germany to the Black Sea resort of Sochi for a holiday which he interrupted on Tuesday to come to Moscow to host Chinese President Jiang Zemin. He looked stiff and tired on Wednesday but appeared to be firmly in control.

Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Itar-Tass news agency last week Yeltsin's holiday was "not linked to medical necessity" and the Kremlin leader would not undergo any special medical treatment in Sochi.
He would go on many walks and, weather permitting, swim, Mironov said. But he did not mention tennis, Yeltsin's favourite sport.
Yeltsin is expected to return to Sochi after talks with the Chinese leader on Thursday and RIA news agency said he would stay there until May 5, when he is due to meet Spanish King Juan Carlos.
